    Stillwater

    A recursive function that you can hear. Every branch is a call with its own voice, and the chord is the live call stack. Step through the calls, play the branches, or hum a tune and grow a tree from it.

    How it works

    Stillwater runs one recursive function. Each call draws a branch, owns a span of time and plays one voice for as long as it is on the stack.

    function grow(call) {
  sound(call);                 // push: a voice enters
  if (isBaseCase(call)) return;  // depth, a pruned cut, or too short to split
  const [early, late] = split(call.time, sway);
  grow(child(call, early, +interval));   // left: rises
  grow(child(call, late,  -interval));   // right: falls
}                              // pop: the voice falls silent

    The chord follows the stack. The trunk spans the whole cycle as a low drone. Its children divide that time. The active branches schedule the notes you hear, from slow harmony near the trunk to quick melody at the leaves. Echoes and releases can linger.

    Parameters. Depth adds voices. Sway sets how each call shares its time, so it shapes both the rhythm and the tree. Spread sets the melodic interval and the stereo width. The seed, a number or any word, makes the variation repeatable.

    Pruning turns a call into a base case. The branch keeps its own note and time while its descendants drop out. Use Undo to restore a tree edit. Listening inside plays one branch as a full cycle.

    Step (or N) runs one call at a time, like a debugger. The markers in grow.js show where each frame is paused, and every step plays that call's note. The score plays the same calls in the same order, spread out over time.

    Hum a tree. Under Plant a melody, hum a tune for a few seconds. Its notes become the leaves of a new tree. The audio stays on your device.

    Drift changes one gene per cycle: one call swaps the direction of its intervals, and every few cycles the key shifts. The breathing guide follows the recursion. Each rise is a left call and each fall is a right call.

    Explore branches

    Choose a call. Hear it, listen inside it, or prune it into a base case.

    Plant a melody

    Hum, sing or whistle for up to 10 seconds, or choose a short clip of one voice or instrument. Stillwater finds the notes on this device and grows a tree that plays them at its leaves.

    Choose a clip or try the built-in example.
